name: Elbow (example)
_UNITS: Every physical value may be written three ways:
3. bare number       "com_distance": 0.28   -> canonical SI assumed, and
flagged in the report's UNIT AUDIT
A unit from the wrong dimension (e.g. kg for a length) is always a hard error.
Set "strict_units": true below to reject form 3 outright.
Canonical units: mass kg, length m, inertia kg.m^2, angle rad, time s,
torque N.m, angular velocity rad/s, temperature degC.
_comment: Two actuators share one joint: torque and mass scale by n, and each unit carries 1/n of the load so each one's thermal problem gets easier. Set ratio if there is a belt or linkage between the actuator output and the joint itself.

ratio.note: actuators mounted coaxially on the joint, no extra reduction

gravity_factor.note: 1 = axis horizontal, link swings against full gravity; 0 = vertical axis

_POWER_SYSTEM: Bus voltage is a property of THIS robot, not of the actuator. The vendor's
rated voltage is only what they characterised the unit at. Set the voltage
your robot actually supplies here; the actuator file declares the range it
will accept, and the two are checked against each other.
Running ABOVE the vendor nominal is routine and simply extends the speed
envelope. Running above their stated MAXIMUM is limited by transistor and
DC-link capacitor voltage ratings rather than by heat, so it cannot be
cleared on thermal grounds; set accept_overvoltage to acknowledge the risk
and downgrade that check from a failure to a warning.
supply_current_limit is optional - omit it if the supply can always deliver
more than the drive's own current rating, which is the usual case.

bus_voltage.note: 13S lithium pack, nominal 48.1 V, 54.6 V at full charge

T_ambient.note: inside the arm shell, NOT room temperature

max_surface_temp.note: housing is reachable by the operator. ISO 13732-1 is the relevant standard for touch-temperature limits; the threshold depends on material and contact duration, so set this from your own safety case rather than treating 48 as a default.
